status: editorial and implementation plan; no live lesson copy changed
basis: src/data/learning.ts and the four stage lesson files

audit.structure: Five units of four lessons. The overall sequence—understand, diagnose, design, test, practice—is sound and can be retained.
audit.depth: All 20 lessons have exactly two teaching paragraphs of roughly 103–135 words combined. Nineteen have one source, one has two. Only the capstone supplies an evidencePacket or detailed assessmentCriteria.
audit.narrative: The primary case changes almost every lesson. The clinic appears at lesson 1 and returns only at lesson 14; the capstone switches to an AI-assisted library service. Repeated context changes consume attention that should go to learning the method.
prerequisites: Lesson 1 discusses system acknowledgment and handoffs before the learner has learned what a task, interface state, or service handoff is.
Lesson 2 names mental models and signifiers in a single paragraph, then moves directly to local save versus remote sync.
Lesson 4 moves from basic trust to AI policy authority and mass messaging, a specialist case too early in the path.
Later lessons assume understanding of triangulation, hypotheses, fidelity, state models, and severity without a definition and demonstration before use.
exerciseEvidence: Lesson 5 asks for five observation notes from a one-sentence scenario with no observation record.
Lesson 8 asks for a statement using call themes that are not supplied.
Lesson 11 asks for roles and publication states without policy or workflow facts.
Lesson 19 asks for an evidence-based decision memo while supplying no evidence.
Several other transfer tasks require learners to invent service behavior; only the capstone gives a substantial fictional evidence packet.
sourceFit: The state-model lesson cites a guide about trust in complex forms rather than state modeling.
The hypothesis lesson cites formative-versus-summative evaluation rather than guidance on forming a testable claim.
The decision-record lesson cites analytics uses rather than a source on communicating a design decision.
The source list appears after the exercise, with no indication of which specific claim or method each source supports.
audit.scopeGap: This is mainly a course in UX reasoning and service decisions. It barely teaches interface structure, information architecture, visual hierarchy, typography, or UI composition. The course description should state its scope; broader UI foundations need a separate planned module or course.

coursePromise: A beginner can follow one realistic service from understanding a person's goal through research, design, testing, and a defensible decision, while learning when a method's evidence is and is not sufficient.
audience: A beginner with no assumed knowledge of UX terminology, research methods, or service design. Familiarity with ordinary websites and mobile apps is enough.

structureDecision.keep: Keep the five-unit, twenty-lesson route and existing IDs for this rewrite so saved progress and navigation remain stable.
structureDecision.positioning: Name this path UX foundations and practice. Do not imply that it is a complete course in UI visual design.
structureDecision.futureGap: Plan a distinct UI foundations path covering layout and hierarchy, typography and color, navigation and information architecture, components and responsive behavior, and accessible visual design. Do not dilute these topics into a paragraph inside the current path.

narrative.runningCase: A fictional outpatient clinic appointment and check-in service: reminder, arrival, identity check, confirmation, waiting, staff handoff, delay, and support.
narrative.caseFacts: Maintain one case dossier with a system diagram, staff process, realistic constraints, observation notes, logs, test sessions, and versions of the proposed flow. Release only the facts needed at each lesson, so learners do not have to invent evidence.
narrative.cumulativeArtifact: Each lesson changes the same learner dossier: goal and task map → interaction/status sketch → barrier review → trust review → observation notes → research plan → cause hypotheses → problem statement → journey and flow → alternatives → state model → prototype brief → hypothesis → test script → findings → revision → staged release plan → service blueprint → decision record.
narrative.transfer: Replace the mandatory new domain in every lesson with a short optional transfer check. Use an independent, fully supplied library case in the capstone to test whether the method transfers.
narrative.fictionRule: Label all invented case evidence as fictional. Distinguish observations from assumptions and never present invented counts as real research.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: What is UX, and what is the patient trying to accomplish?
teachBeforeUse: person, goal, task, touchpoint, interface versus service
lessonProgression.caseMove: Follow an appointment from reminder to confirmed arrival, including what happens outside the kiosk.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Goal and task-boundary map.
lessonProgression.bridge: A mapped task creates the need to understand what each interaction communicates.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: How does a patient know what action is possible and whether it succeeded?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Compare the kiosk's visible 'Done' message with actual receipt by the appointment system.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Simple before/during/after status sketch.
lessonProgression.bridge: Status is useful only if different people can perceive and act on it.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: Who is blocked from the same task, and where?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Review check-in in a noisy, bright lobby with reach, language, time, and privacy constraints.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Barrier map and alternative completion routes.
lessonProgression.bridge: An accessible path also has to make truthful promises about personal information and outcomes.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: What must a patient understand before sharing information or relying on confirmation?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Explain identity questions, sensitive information, receipt, and how a patient can correct a mistake.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Trust and consequence review.
lessonProgression.bridge: The team now has assumptions about the experience; the next unit observes what happens.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: What did people actually do at check-in?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Give a timed fictional observation transcript including lobby events, staff help, and kiosk state.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Marked observation notes and unanswered questions.
lessonProgression.bridge: Observations reveal uncertainties that require a suitable method.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: Which evidence could distinguish a confusing message from a failed handoff?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Compare a check-in completion event, staff receipt log, support notes, and interviews; show what each cannot prove.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Question-to-evidence plan.
lessonProgression.bridge: Once evidence arrives, several explanations may still fit.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: Why did a patient ask staff whether check-in worked?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Provide a small evidence packet with a delay, a kiosk message, and a staff queue event. Compare plausible causes.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Cause hypotheses and targeted checks.
lessonProgression.bridge: The team can now state a problem without claiming an unproven cause.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: What problem is supported strongly enough to design against?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Use the accumulated fictional evidence to frame the patient's and staff's problem without prescribing a new screen.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Revisable problem statement and evidence ledger.
lessonProgression.bridge: The design unit must connect a response to the whole service, not just the kiosk.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: Where can the service lose the patient between arrival and care?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Trace patient, kiosk, receptionist, and appointment system through successful and interrupted check-in.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Current and proposed journey plus one detailed task flow.
lessonProgression.bridge: A mapped failure point permits multiple design approaches.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: Which confirmation approach fits the clinic's people and constraints?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Compare kiosk receipt, staffed confirmation, and optional phone confirmation using the same evidence and access constraints.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Alternatives table and provisional choice.
lessonProgression.bridge: The chosen approach needs behavior for every consequential state.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: What happens before receipt, after receipt, and when receipt fails?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Specify idle, entered, submitting, received, delayed, failed, and reset states without claiming success early.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Annotated state model and status language.
lessonProgression.bridge: A prototype must represent the states needed to test the choice.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: What is the smallest prototype that can answer the current design question?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Prototype kiosk messages and a staff acknowledgment delay; list what is simulated and what real integration must test later.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Prototype brief and study-ready flow.
lessonProgression.bridge: The evaluation unit states what change the prototype is expected to cause.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: What would count as improvement, and what might get worse?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Predict that receipt-backed wording reduces repeat check-in and unnecessary staff queries, while checking for slower completion.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Hypothesis and observation criteria.
lessonProgression.bridge: The hypothesis determines the study task and conditions.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: How can the clinic observe whether patients understand the status?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Write a lobby task that does not tell participants to use the kiosk; include delayed receipt and accessible routes.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Test plan, tasks, and note template.
lessonProgression.bridge: The team needs a disciplined way to interpret the resulting observations.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: Which conclusions do the observations support?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Supply fictional participant notes, comments, staff events, and system logs, including one contradictory case.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Finding cards with evidence and uncertainty.
lessonProgression.bridge: A finding suggests a revision, which must itself be tested.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: Which change addresses the observed failure, and how could it fail?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Revise delayed and confirmed messages, then test both original confusion and any new delay or privacy cost.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Findings-to-changes table and retest plan.
lessonProgression.bridge: A working design still needs a feasible release and operational owner.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: What can the clinic safely improve before its old system is replaced?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Stage copy, reception process, and later system acknowledgment; specify what cannot be promised yet.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Staged release decision with owners and checks.
lessonProgression.bridge: The interim route must work across the channels patients actually use.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: Will kiosk, phone, messages, and staff give compatible answers?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Blueprint the same appointment status through kiosk, reception, SMS, and phone support, including an outage.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Service blueprint fragment and recovery owner.
lessonProgression.bridge: The team needs a concise record of why the coordinated approach was chosen.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: Can another team member understand and revisit this decision?
lessonProgression.caseMove: Write a one-page recommendation for receipt-backed confirmation with an interim outage path.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Decision record connected to earlier artifacts.
lessonProgression.bridge: The capstone tests the whole chain in a new service.

lessonProgression.learnerQuestion: Can the learner transfer the process to a different service without invented facts?
teachBeforeUse: recap of the complete method, no new specialist topic
lessonProgression.caseMove: Use a new fictional library reservation case with a complete, internally consistent evidence and constraint packet. Remove AI as a required topic unless an optional extension is provided.
lessonProgression.dossierAddition: Independent case dossier: map, observations, problem, alternatives, states, test, and decision.
lessonProgression.bridge: End with reflection on what evidence is still needed, not a claim of certification.

lessonContentContract.opening: A concrete scene and a question the learner can answer after the lesson.
lessonContentContract.concepts: Introduce at most two major new terms at a time; define each before use and show the term in the running case.
lessonContentContract.method: A short sequence of observable steps, including when to use it, when not to, and what it cannot establish.
lessonContentContract.workedExample: Walk through evidence → interpretation → action, exposing the reasoning and any uncertainty rather than presenting an expert verdict.
lessonContentContract.guidedPractice: Give a bounded evidence packet and explain feedback against stated criteria. Avoid a hidden correct answer when evidence cannot distinguish options.
lessonContentContract.independentWork: Provide the facts, constraints, and material needed to make the requested artifact. Ask learners to mark assumptions instead of inventing observations or policy.
lessonContentContract.bridge: End with what the artifact established, what remains unknown, and why the next lesson follows.
lessonContentContract.references: Place 2–4 relevant readings beside the claims or method they support, with publisher, author/date when available, and a one-line reason to read each. Treat the 4,830-URL index as discovery data, not authority.

siteUpdatePlan.name: Select and verify evidence
siteUpdatePlan.work: For each lesson, read candidate articles, record claim-to-source links, author/date, evidence type, limitations, and access status. Keep only sources that directly teach the lesson's method; supplement the 29-source map with strong articles from the fetched corpus. Do not paste article text into the site.
siteUpdatePlan.deliverable: Reviewed source ledger for all 20 lessons and a clean reading list.

siteUpdatePlan.name: Build the fictional case dossier
siteUpdatePlan.work: Write one internally consistent timeline, service state diagram, staff process, access constraints, research notes, logs, prototype observations, and test results. Reveal the packet progressively by lesson.
siteUpdatePlan.deliverable: Case assets and evidence packets that make exercises answerable without invented facts.

siteUpdatePlan.name: Extend the lesson data model
siteUpdatePlan.work: Replace the two-paragraph-only teaching field with typed sections for opening, defined terms, method steps, worked reasoning, evidence, checkpoint, bridge, and claim-level citations. Preserve existing lesson IDs and progress keys. Update the current lesson template to render the added depth within its existing visual design.
siteUpdatePlan.deliverable: A reusable course content structure and one complete pilot lesson.

siteUpdatePlan.name: Rewrite and review sequentially
siteUpdatePlan.work: Produce units 1 through 5 in order. Review each unit for factual accuracy, beginner comprehension, source fit, cross-lesson continuity, task answerability, and response feedback before moving on. Edit manually for voice and precision; reject generic filler and unexplained jargon.
siteUpdatePlan.deliverable: Twenty revised lessons and cumulative learner artifacts.

siteUpdatePlan.name: Validate before replacing live copy
siteUpdatePlan.work: Run structural checks, inspect all lesson pages on desktop and mobile, and run comprehension sessions with novices using representative lessons from each unit. Fix misunderstandings before publication; then measure lesson progression and task completion alongside exits.
siteUpdatePlan.deliverable: Verified course release with documented remaining limitations.

releaseCriteria: A novice can explain each new term after its first use and identify why it matters in the running case.
Every exercise can be completed from supplied information or clearly asks the learner to name what must be researched.
Each worked example traces a specific piece of evidence to an interpretation and an action, with uncertainty marked.
Each key factual or methodological claim has a directly relevant reading; sources are linked at the point of use.
No copied article bodies, unsourced invented research results, or fabricated real-world statistics appear in lesson copy.
The output of each lesson supplies the starting material for the next lesson in its unit and across unit boundaries.
The capstone teaches no new required specialist concepts and can be completed using its supplied dossier.
Existing lesson URLs and browser progress remain valid after the content migration.
